vsm2.14:59.1: 12. The life faculty has the characteristic of maintaining conascent kinds of matter.
vsm2.14:59.2: Its function is to make them occur.
vsm2.14:59.3: It is manifested in the establishing of their presence.
vsm2.14:59.4: Its proximate cause is primary elements that are to be sustained.
vsm2.14:59.5:
And although it has the capacity consisting in the characteristic of maintaining, etc., yet it only maintains
conascent kinds of matter at the moment of presence, as water does lotuses and so on.
vsm2.14:59.6: Though states (dhamma) arise due to their own conditions, it maintains them, as a wet-nurse does a prince.
vsm2.14:59.7: And it occurs itself only through its connection with the states that occur, like a pilot;
vsm2.14:59.8: it does not cause occurrence after dissolution, because of its own absence and that of what has to be made to occur.
vsm2.14:59.9: It does not prolong presence at the moment of dissolution because it is itself dissolving,
vsm2.14:59.10: like the flame of a lamp when the wick and the oil are getting used up.
vsm2.14:59.11:
But it must not be regarded as destitute of power to maintain, make occur, and make present,
because it does accomplish each of these functions at the moment stated (cf. Dhs §635).
vsm2.14:60.1:
13. The heart-basis has the characteristic of being the (material)
support for the mind-element and for the mind-consciousness-element.
vsm2.14:60.2: Its function is to observe them.
vsm2.14:60.3: It is manifested as the carrying of them.
vsm2.14:60.4:
It is to be found in dependence on the blood, of the kind described in the treatise
on mindfulness of the body (VIII.111), inside the heart.
vsm2.14:60.5:
It is assisted by the primaries with their functions of upholding, etc.; it is consolidated by temperature,
consciousness, and nutriment; it is maintained by life;
vsm2.14:60.6: and it serves as physical basis for the mind-element and mind-consciousness-element, and for the states associated with them.
vsm2.14:61.1:
14. Bodily intimation is the mode (conformation) and the alteration (deformation) in the consciousness-originated
air element that causes the occurrence of moving forward, etc., which mode and alteration
are a condition for the stiffening, upholding, and moving of the conascent material body.
vsm2.14:61.2: Its function is to display intention.
vsm2.14:61.3: It is manifested as the cause of bodily excitement.
vsm2.14:61.4: Its proximate cause is the consciousness-originated air element.
vsm2.14:61.5:
But it is called "bodily intimation" (kāyaviññatti) because it is the cause of the intimating (viññāpana) of intention by means
of bodily excitement, and because it is itself intimatable through the body, in other words, through that bodily excitement.
vsm2.14:61.6:
Moving forward, etc., should be understood to occur owing to the movement of the kinds of matter that are temperature-born,
etc., which are interlocked with the consciousness-born kinds moved by that intimation (See Dhs §636).
vsm2.14:62.1:
15. Verbal intimation is the mode (conformation) and the alteration (deformation) in the consciousness-originated earth element that
causes that occurrence of speech utterance which mode and alteration are a condition for the knocking together of clung-to matter.
vsm2.14:62.2: Its function is to display intention.
vsm2.14:62.3: It is manifested as the cause of the voice in speech.
vsm2.14:62.4: Its proximate cause is the consciousness-originated earth element.
vsm2.14:62.5:
But it is called "verbal intimation" because it is the cause of the intimating of intention by means of the voice in speech,
and because it is itself intimatable through speech, in other words, through that voice in speech.
vsm2.14:62.6:
For, just as, on seeing a sign for water consisting of an ox skull, etc., hung up in the forest, it is intimated that "there
is water here," so too, on noticing either the bodily shaking or the voice in speech thus, they intimate. (See Dhs §637.)
vsm2.14:63.1: 16. The space element has the characteristic of delimiting matter.
vsm2.14:63.2: Its function is to display the boundaries of matter.
vsm2.14:63.3: It is manifested as the confines of matter; or it is manifested as untouchedness, as the state of gaps and apertures (cf. Dhs §638).
vsm2.14:63.4: Its proximate cause is the matter delimited.
vsm2.14:63.5: And it is on account of it that one can say of material things delimited that "this is above, below, around, that."
vsm2.14:64.1: 17. Lightness of matter has the characteristic of non-slowness.
vsm2.14:64.2: Its function is to dispel heaviness of matter.
vsm2.14:64.3: It is manifested as light transformability.
vsm2.14:64.4: Its proximate cause is light matter (cf. Dhs §639).
vsm2.14:64.5: 18. Malleability of matter has the characteristic of non-stiffenedness.
vsm2.14:64.6: Its function is to dispel stiffness of matter.
vsm2.14:64.7: It is manifested as non-opposition to any kind of action.
vsm2.14:64.8: Its proximate cause is malleable matter (cf. Dhs §640).
vsm2.14:64.9: 19. Wieldiness of matter has the characteristic of wieldiness that is favourable to bodily action.
vsm2.14:64.10: Its function is to dispel unwieldiness.
vsm2.14:64.12: Its proximate cause is wieldy matter (cf. Dhs §641).
vsm2.14:65.1: These three, however, are not found apart from each other.
vsm2.14:65.2:
Still their difference may be understood as follows. Lightness of matter is alteration of matter such as any light (agile)
state in material instances, as in one who is healthy, any non-slowness, any manner of light transformability in them,
which is originated by conditions that prevent any disturbance of elements capable of creating sluggishness of matter.
vsm2.14:65.3:
Malleability of matter is alteration of matter such as any malleable state in material instances, as in a well-pounded hide,
any pliable manner consisting in amenableness to exercise of power over them in all kinds of work without distinction,
which is originated by conditions that prevent any disturbance of elements capable of creating stiffness of matter.
vsm2.14:65.4:
Wieldiness of matter is alteration of matter such as any wieldy state in material instances, as in well-refined gold,
any manner in them consisting in favourableness to the work of the body, which is originated by conditions
that prevent any disturbance of elements capable of creating unfavourableness to the work of the body.
vsm2.14:66.1: 20. Growth of matter has the characteristic of setting up.
vsm2.14:66.2: Its function is to make material instances emerge in the first instance.
vsm2.14:66.3: It is manifested as launching; or it is manifested as the completed state.
vsm2.14:66.4: Its proximate cause is grown matter.
vsm2.14:66.5: 21. Continuity of matter has the characteristic of occurrence.
vsm2.14:66.8: Its proximate cause is matter that is to be anchored.
vsm2.14:66.9:
Both of these are terms for matter at its birth; but owing to difference of mode, and according to different persons' susceptibility
to instruction, the teaching in the summary (uddesa) in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī is given as "growth and continuity" (cf. Dhs §596);
vsm2.14:66.10:
but since there is here no difference in meaning, consequently in the description (niddesa) of these words, "the setting
up of the sense-bases is the growth of matter" and "the growth of matter is the continuity of matter" is said (Dhs §642, 732, 865).
vsm2.14:67.1:
And in the Commentary, after saying, "It is genesis that is called 'setting up,' increase
that is called 'growth,' occurrence that is called 'continuity,'"
vsm2.14:67.2:
this simile is given: "Genesis as setting up is like the time when water comes up in a hole dug in a river bank;
increase as growth is like the time when it fills the hole; occurrence as continuity is like the time when it overflows."
vsm2.14:67.3:
And at the end of the simile it is said: "So what is stated? Setting up
is stated by sense-base; sense-base is stated by setting up."
vsm2.14:67.4: Consequently, it is the first genesis of material instances that is their setting up;
vsm2.14:67.5: the genesis also of others that are generated in addition to those is growth since it appears in the aspect of increase;
vsm2.14:67.6:
the repeated genesis also of others that are generated in addition to those is continuity since it
appears in the aspect of anchoring. This is how it should be understood to have been declared thus.
vsm2.14:68.1: 22. Ageing has the characteristic of maturing (ripening) material instances.
vsm2.14:68.2: Its function is to lead on towards their termination.
vsm2.14:68.3: It is manifested as the loss of newness without the loss of individual essence, like oldness in paddy.
vsm2.14:68.4: Its proximate cause is matter that is maturing (ripening).
vsm2.14:68.5:
This is said with reference to the kind of ageing that is evident through seeing alteration in teeth,
etc., as their brokenness, and so on (cf. Dhs §644).
vsm2.14:68.6: But that of immaterial states, which has no such visible alteration, is called hidden ageing.
vsm2.14:68.7: And that in earth, water, rocks, the moon, the sun, etc., is called incessant ageing.
vsm2.14:69.1: 23. Impermanence of matter has the characteristic of complete breaking up.
vsm2.14:69.2: Its function is to make material instances subside.
vsm2.14:69.3: It is manifested as destruction and fall (cf. Dhs §645).
vsm2.14:69.4: Its proximate cause is matter that is completely breaking up.
vsm2.14:70.1: 24. Physical nutriment has the characteristic of nutritive essence.
vsm2.14:70.2: Its function is to feed kinds of matter.
vsm2.14:70.4: Its proximate cause is a physical basis that must be fed with physical food.
vsm2.14:70.5: It is a term for the nutritive essence by means of which living beings sustain themselves (cf. Dhs §646).
vsm2.14:71.1: These, firstly, are the material instances that have been handed down in the texts.
vsm2.14:71.2:
But in the Commentary, others have been added as follows: matter as power, matter as procreation,
matter as birth, matter as sickness; and, in the opinion of some, matter as torpor.
vsm2.14:71.3:
In the first place, matter as torpor is rejected as non-existent by the words:
Surely thou art a sage enlightened, There are no hindrances in thee (Sn 541).
vsm2.14:71.4:
As to the rest, matter as sickness is included by ageing and by impermanence; matter as birth by growth and continuity;
matter as procreation, by the water element; and matter as power by the air element.
vsm2.14:71.5: So taken separately not even one of these exists: this was the agreement reached.
vsm2.14:71.6:
So this derived matter of twenty-four sorts and the aforesaid matter of the primary elements,
which is of four sorts, together amount to twenty-eight sorts, neither more nor less.
vsm2.14:72.1:
And all that matter of twenty-eight sorts is of one kind as "not-root-cause, root-causeless,
dissociated from root-cause, with conditions, mundane, subject to cankers" (Dhs §584), and so on.
vsm2.14:72.2:
It is of two kinds as internal and external, gross and subtle, far and near, produced (nipphanna) and unproduced,
sensitive matter and insensitive matter, faculty and non-faculty, clung to and not-clung to, and so on.
vsm2.14:73.1:
Herein, the five kinds beginning with the eye are internal because they occur as an integral part of the selfhood (in oneself);
the rest are external because they are external to that selfhood (personality).
vsm2.14:73.2:
The nine beginning with the eye and the three elements excepting the water element, making twelve kinds in all,
are to be taken as gross because of impinging; the rest are subtle because they are the opposite of that.
vsm2.14:73.3: What is subtle is far because it is difficult to penetrate, the other is near because it is easy to penetrate.
vsm2.14:73.4:
The eighteen kinds of matter, that is to say, the four elements, the thirteen beginning with the eye, and physical nutriment,
are produced because they can be discerned through their own individual essences, having exceeded the purely conceptual states of
matter as delimitation, matter as alteration, and matter as characteristic (see §77); the rest, being the opposite, are unproduced.
vsm2.14:73.6:
Sensitive matter itself, together with the three beginning with the femininity faculty,
is faculty in the sense of predominance; the rest are not-faculty because they are the opposite of that.
vsm2.14:73.7:
What we shall later describe as "kamma-born" (§75 and XX.27) is clung to because that is "clung to," that is, acquired by kamma.
The rest are not-clung to because they are the opposite of that.
vsm2.14:74.1: Again, all matter is of three kinds according to the visible (sanidassana) triad, the kamma-born triad, etc. (see Dhs 2).
vsm2.14:74.2: Herein, as regards the gross, a visible datum is visible with impact; the rest are invisible with impact;
vsm2.14:74.3: all the subtle kinds are invisible without impact.
vsm2.14:74.4: So firstly it is of three kinds according to the visible triad.
vsm2.14:75.1:
According to the kamma-born triad, etc., however, that born from kamma is kamma-born; that born from a condition
other than that is not-kamma-born; that not born from anything is neither-kamma-born-nor-not-kamma-born.
vsm2.14:75.2:
That born from consciousness is consciousness-born; that born from a condition other than consciousness
is not-consciousness-born; that not born from anything is neither-consciousness-born-nor-not-consciousness-born.
vsm2.14:75.3:
That born from nutriment is nutriment-born; that born from a condition other than that is not-nutriment-born;
that not born from anything is neither-nutriment-born-nor-not-nutriment-born.
vsm2.14:75.4:
That born from temperature is temperature-born; that born from a condition other than that is not-temperature-born;
that not born from anything is neither-temperature-born-nor-not-temperature-born.
vsm2.14:75.5: So it is of three kinds according to the kamma-born triad, and so on.
vsm2.14:76.1: Again, it is of four kinds as seen, etc., as concrete matter, etc., and as the physical basis tetrads, and so on.
vsm2.14:76.2: Herein, the visible-data base is seen because it is the objective field of seeing.
vsm2.14:76.3: The sound base is heard because it is the objective field of hearing.
vsm2.14:76.4:
The three, that is to say, odours, flavours, and tangible data, are sensed (lit. contacted) because
they are the objective fields of faculties that take contiguous objective fields.
vsm2.14:76.5: The rest are cognized because they are the objective field of consciousness (cognition) only.
vsm2.14:76.6: So firstly it is of four kinds according to the seen, etc., tetrad.
vsm2.14:77.1: Here, however, "produced matter" is concrete matter;
vsm2.14:77.3: those from "bodily intimation" up to "wieldiness" are matter as alteration;
vsm2.14:77.4: birth, ageing and dissolution are matter as characteristic.
vsm2.14:77.5: So it is of four kinds as concrete matter and so on.
vsm2.14:78.1: Here, however, what is called the materiality of the heart is physical basis, not door (see Dhs-a 82f.);
vsm2.14:78.2: the two intimations are door, not physical basis;
vsm2.14:78.3: sensitive matter is both physical basis and door;
vsm2.14:78.4: the rest are neither physical basis nor door.
vsm2.14:78.5: So it is four kinds according to the physical basis tetrad.
vsm2.14:79.1: Again, it is of five kinds as born of one, born of two, born of three, born of four, and not born of anything.
vsm2.14:79.2: Herein, what is kamma-born only or consciousness-born only is called born of one.
vsm2.14:79.3: Of these, materiality of the faculties, together with the heart-basis, is kamma-born only;
vsm2.14:79.4: the two intimations are consciousness-born only.
vsm2.14:79.5: But what is born now of consciousness and now of temperature is called born of two. That is the sound base only.
vsm2.14:79.6:
What is born of temperature, consciousness, and nutriment is called
born of three. But that is the three beginning with "lightness" only.
vsm2.14:79.7: What is born from the four beginning with kamma is called born of four. That is all the rest except "matter as characteristic."
vsm2.14:80.1: But "matter as characteristic" is called not born of anything.
vsm2.14:80.3: Because there is no arising of arising, and the other two are the mere maturing and breakup of what has arisen.
vsm2.14:80.4:
Though in the passage, "The visible-data base, the sound base, the odour base, the flavour base, the tangible-data base,
the space element, the water element, lightness of matter, malleability of matter, wieldiness of matter,
growth of matter, continuity of matter, and physical food—these states are consciousness-originated" (cf.
Dhs §667) and so on, a state of birth that is, growth being born from somewhere can be understood as allowable
vsm2.14:80.5:
since the point of view here is the moment when the conditions that are giving
birth to the kinds of materiality are exercising their function.
vsm2.14:80.6: This, firstly, is the section of the detailed explanation dealing with the materiality aggregate.
